snippet.title: I Tested The Viral Github Repo That Reverse Engineers Anything
snippet.description:
🔥 Join Maker School & get customer #1 guaranteed: https://skool.com/makerschool/about
💎 Get all course resources 100% free: https://skool.com/maker-zero/about
➡️ If this is your first video: I'm Nick Saraev. I run LeftClick, an AI growth agency. We've done work for large brands you're likely familiar with, like Mr. Beast, Anthropic, OpenAI, and a few others.

In plain English: I help people build systems that generate leads, close deals, and scale businesses, mostly using new AI models like Claude. I also make videos about how to do all of that here on YouTube.

It hasn't always been this way. My family immigrated from a Soviet bloc country (People's Republic of Bulgaria) in the 90s. They worked extremely hard, and we were broke for a very long time. I grew up wishing for more security, stability, and freedom over my own life.

I don't have a programming degree, and never took formal education for IT or workflows. I learned it all myself from YouTube videos like you're watching now.

As for my path: I started my first business at 19 in college. We threw events (mostly parties) at campus bars, and charged people for entry. 

That failed to provide me enough money to pay my bills, so at 21, I started another business, a door-to-door marketing agency.

From there, every year, I would start several companies, over 10 in total. I did this in a variety of industries, like e-commerce, photography, videography, SaaS, credit repair, etc. Each grew slightly more profitable, until, at 25, I would start 1SecondCopy, a content writing company. A friend and I eventually scaled that to over $90,000/m. It was my first taste of financial independence, and the reason I'm here today.

Since starting my journey, I've grown a fair bit of capital. To diversify my income, at 30, I began investing in other businesses and advising companies on how to grow in the AI era. These include SaaS businesses, like Clairvo, agencies like Dental Connect, and more. 

Collectively, the businesses that I own outright or are a part of generate over $10 million per year. This returns far more than the 5-10% you would get in the stock market, but also requires a lot of my active time. There's a tradeoff there, but I greatly prefer active investing, where I have control over the entities I'm a part of.

It wasn't easy to get here. But I did in the end! For anyone on their own entrepreneurial journey: I wish you luck, happiness, and perseverance. You can make it!

Summary ⤵️
The end-to-end, definitive course on Claude Code for beginners! I'll take you through a full four-hour masterclass where I start by teaching you how to set up and install Claude Code in a tutorial, how to configure your IDE or integrated development environment (we'll use Antigravity), how to utilize your CLAUDE.md file as your project brain, how to build your first project in Antigravity using Claude Code in under 15 minutes, advanced Claude Code functionality including hooks, slash commands, and more. 

I also teach you how to spin up multiple Claude Code instances and have them work on your behalf; how to parallelize work using sub-agents; how to use Git work trees to accomplish many hours of work in just a few minutes; how to conserve tokens and use context management to crush your coding and software projects; how to deploy things to the cloud using Modal and related services, and in general... how to be awesome at Claude Code! Hope you enjoy the tutorial.

1:08 How REA Works
2:44 Rebuilding Preview
4:46 Matching the App
5:26 Not Exactly New
7:27 What It Means Next

Most people open #ChatGPT Work, type a question, and end up using it exactly like the regular chatbot. In this tutorial I show you the one thing that changes that: a folder you mount, with a plain-English rulebook inside that ChatGPT Work reads before every single task.

You'll set that up, teach it rules it actually remembers, connect Plugins like Gmail and Google Calendar, and build a Skill that learns from your own edits. And if you already use #Claude Cowork, the same folder works in both, so this is an #AI system you only build once.

snippet.title: What Is Grok Bot? Grok Bot vs ChatGPT & Claude Explained #GrokBot #Grok #AIAgents #AI
snippet.description:
What is Grok Bot, and is it really different from ChatGPT or Claude? Here's Grok Bot explained simply, for beginners.

Instead of one AI chatbot, xAI's Grok Bot lets you set up a team of AI workers ("Bots"), each with its own job. They can talk to each other, hand work off, and use websites and apps on a shared cloud computer. You can even teach a Bot a task by doing the steps once while it watches.

But ChatGPT and Claude can already do much more than answer questions. They're becoming AI agents too. So the bigger question may not be which AI is best. It may be: how much work are you comfortable handing over to AI?

In this Short:
- What Grok Bot is and how Grok Bots work together
- Teaching a Bot a task by showing it
- Grok Bot vs ChatGPT and Claude: what's actually different

Grok Bot is in beta. Availability and pricing vary by plan and may change. This information is current as of September 2026.

Sources (xAI):
- Introducing Grok Bot: https://x.ai/news/introducing-grok-bot
- Grok Bot documentation: https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/overview

This is AI Uncomplicated, and it is just that simple.

snippet.description:
What does it really take to become an AI-ready Business Analyst in 2026?
AI is changing how Business Analysts research, analyse, document, communicate and deliver solutions. But knowing ChatGPT alone isn't enough.

In this video, Dibhanshu Saurav breaks down a practical AI Business Analyst Roadmap for 2026 using a 4-level AI competency framework — from understanding AI fundamentals to leveraging AI tools, using specialized AI solutions, and eventually building AI automation and agentic workflows.

You'll understand what companies expect from Business Analysts in the AI era, which AI skills actually matter, how far a BA needs to go with AI, and where the role starts to overlap with AI/ML Engineering.

In this video, you'll learn:

• What an AI-ready Business Analyst looks like in 2026
• What companies expect from AI Business Analysts
• The 4 levels of AI competency for Business Analysts
• AI fundamentals every BA should understand
• How Business Analysts can use AI for research, analysis and documentation
• Generic AI tools vs. specialized AI tools
• AI-powered BA workflows and real-time deliverables
• AI automation and Agentic AI for Business Analysts
• AI Business Analyst vs. AI/ML Engineer roles
• Where a Business Analyst's responsibility ends in AI projects
• How to build your AI skills strategically instead of trying to learn everything

The goal isn't to turn every Business Analyst into an AI/ML Engineer.

The goal is to become an AI-infused Business Analyst who knows how to leverage AI to solve business problems better, faster and more effectively.

snippet.title: How I Stopped Re-Explaining My Business to AI Every Single Time
snippet.description:
🚀 Try Vida AI: https://vida.app/

What if your AI already understood your work context before you even asked a question?

In this video, I test Vida AI using a real task from my business: responding to an actual brand partner without manually copying and pasting previous emails, briefs, documents, and project history into an AI chat first.

The challenge with most AI tools is context. Before asking for help, you often have to explain everything again—upload the relevant files, paste previous conversations, provide background information, and then finally ask your question.

Vida is designed to approach this differently by connecting relevant files, project history, work context, and cross-application information, allowing its AI assistant to potentially understand more about the task you're working on without requiring you to manually provide everything again.

To test it, I use a genuine brand-partner email from my own business and ask Vida to draft a response without manually feeding it the original brief or previous conversation.

I also look at the bigger questions surrounding AI assistants with persistent work context, including privacy, data handling, human review, and whether an AI can genuinely become more useful as it understands more about how you work.

⏱️ TIMESTAMPS

01:00 What Vida AI Actually Does

You’ll start with analytics fundamentals (descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, prescriptive) and Excel as an analytics platform, then move into hands-on data preparation: importing from CSV/JSON/SQL, cleaning duplicates, text normalization, and data validation. The course teaches core Excel skills—cell references, logical/lookup/statistical functions, PivotTables, Power Query ETL, and Power Pivot data models—before layering AI capabilities like Analyze Data, Smart Insights, forecasting, and ChatGPT/Copilot integration to automate analysis and narrate findings.

Real-world projects span sales, finance, marketing, and operations, culminating in interactive KPI dashboards and business reports. By the end, you’ll be able to automate routine analysis, uncover hidden trends, and present actionable insights that drive smarter business decisions in 2026.

snippet.title: After Capitalism: A Cooperative Economy (Documentary)
snippet.description:
Many of us have heard the term "co-op", but what does it really mean? 

This documentary explores what cooperative businesses are and the benefits they bring to workers, consumers, and the community as a whole. It focuses on Baltimore, MD - one of the cities leading the nation's cooperative movement. 

A cooperative economy is an economy that works better for everyone, not just for a few at the top. Hear the stories of the people building one.

This project exists to explore and highlight tangible ways of resisting the oppressive nature of capitalism. It is designed to both instill hope in viewers that more harmonious and equitable alternatives exist while also educating about what those alternatives are, how they function within the economic system as it stands, and how we can replicate them.

snippet.description:
A 36-minute documentary has sparked a much bigger debate about political power, corporate influence, and the future of Indian democracy. Behind the headlines lies a story involving major business deals, government decisions, public resources, and controversies surrounding the relationship between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and billionaire businessman Gautam Adani.

The Friendship Files brings attention to questions surrounding the growth of the Adani Group, its expansion across strategic sectors, and the political and economic controversies that have attracted national and international attention.

🔎 WHAT DOES THIS STORY REVEAL?

▪️ The Modi–Adani Relationship: The relationship between Narendra Modi and Gautam Adani, and why it has become a subject of national and international debate.

▪️ Land Allocations and Government Policies: Land allotments, public resources, and government policies connected to large infrastructure and industrial projects.

▪️ Ports, Coal and Energy: The expansion of the Adani Group across ports, coal, power, and other strategic sectors, alongside questions about government decisions and contracts.

▪️ The Airport Privatisation Controversy: The award of six airports to the Adani Group, changes to bidding rules, and concerns raised about competition and transparency.

▪️ The Mumbai Airport Dispute: The GVK–Adani controversy, the circumstances surrounding the transfer of control, and the questions raised about the process.

▪️ NDTV and Media Ownership: The Adani Group's acquisition of NDTV and the wider debate over media independence, corporate ownership, and press freedom.

▪️ The Mundra Port Drug Seizure: The massive heroin seizure at Mundra Port, the subsequent investigation, and questions surrounding accountability.

▪️ Land and Business Expansion in Bihar: Land, industrial projects, and questions about the relationship between private investment and public interest.

▪️ LIC and Public Money: The Life Insurance Corporation's exposure to Adani Group companies and concerns surrounding public-sector investments and financial risks.

▪️ International Projects: Adani's overseas expansion and the controversies and political questions surrounding major projects outside India.

▪️ The Bigger Picture: Corporate influence, government accountability, public assets, independent journalism, and the relationship between political power and private business interests.

From land and infrastructure to energy, airports, media ownership, and public-sector investments, these controversies raise fundamental questions about transparency, competition, and accountability.

When a business group expands across critical sectors of the economy, what role do government policies play? How are major public decisions made? Who benefits from the use of public resources? And what safeguards ensure that powerful businesses and political institutions remain accountable?

The debate surrounding Modi and Adani goes beyond two influential individuals. It touches on the functioning of public institutions, the role of independent journalism, the protection of public assets, and the importance of transparency in a democracy.

snippet.title: # The Economics of Owning a Film Studio
snippet.description:
The Economics of Owning a Film Studio
**What really happens when a movie makes $677 million at the box office—and the person who wrote the original story gets paid nothing?**

Most people think owning a film studio means greenlighting blockbusters and watching the profits roll in. snippet.title: The Economics Behind Home Depot | Business Strategy Documentary
snippet.description:
Most people think Home Depot makes money by selling paint, tools, and lumber to homeowners. The real story is bigger.

In 2024 and 2025, this retail giant spent over $23 billion acquiring specialty distribution companies most shoppers have never heard of — SRS Distribution, GMS, and Mingledorff's. This video breaks down why.

We dig into the fiscal 2025 numbers: $164.7 billion in revenue, a 33.3% gross margin, and $14.2 billion in net earnings — even as high interest rates slowed consumer renovation spending. Comparable sales grew just 0.3%, forcing a strategic shift toward professional contractors instead of everyday shoppers.

Here's what you'll learn:

• How gross margin, operating income, and services revenue actually work together
• Why the Pro customer segment (9 million contractors, $90B+ in spending) matters more than foot traffic
• What SRS, GMS, and HVAC distribution add to the business model
• Why the company is targeting a $1.2 trillion addressable market
• How installation services and trade credit create repeat business

This isn't a story about hardware stores. It's about supply chains, contractor relationships, and controlling more of the construction economy — not just the shelf.

If you're into business strategy, corporate acquisitions, retail economics, or how public companies actually generate profit, this breakdown is for you.

🔔 Subscribe for more deep dives into how major companies really make money.

snippet.title: Forging the Trillion Dollar Space Economy | True Story Documentary Channel
snippet.description: About the people, perils and promises behind the emerging space industry. Sparked by humanity’s unquenchable thirst for exploration, fuelled by capitalism’s insatiable hunger for profits and propelled by breathtaking technological advances, a New Space Renaissance is emerging. Fortitude uncovers how a few influential individuals with utopian ideas and vast fortunes are forging a trillion-dollar off-world industry, while inspiring millions of us back on Earth. This is the story of those who take the risks, invest the capital, and endeavor to turn science fiction into science fact. Follow award-winning filmmaker Torsten Hoffmann as he candidly meets leaders in the emerging space industry, including policy makers from the United Nations, renowned astrophysicist Neil de Grasse Tyson, leading venture capitalists, established technology companies such as Northrop Grumman and Viasat as well as ambitious start-ups such as Planet, Voyager Space, Privateer, Astroscale and many more. The film highlights that a new space age has dawned and challenges viewers to question the economic viability of the most hyped projects, sustainability way beyond planet Earth and billionaire bravado.

snippet.title: Suharto: The Billions That Disappeared From Indonesia   Economic Horizon | Documentary Script |
snippet.description:
What happens when a nation’s wealth gathers around its ruler and inner circle?

For 32 years, Suharto led Indonesia. His New Order government delivered real economic growth and a sharp fall in poverty, but it was also surrounded by one of the most debated corruption controversies in modern history. Transparency International has estimated that $15–35 billion may have been misappropriated by Suharto and those around him. This is an estimate of alleged misappropriation, not an amount proven in court.

In this documentary, we look at:

How Suharto rose to power and what the New Order achieved
How nepotism, privileged contracts, and politically connected businesses are alleged to have worked
The hidden economic cost of favoritism: lost competition, weaker public trust, and opportunity cost
The 1997–98 Asian financial crisis, and why corruption made Indonesia more vulnerable without being the only cause
Suharto’s resignation in May 1998, and the difference between allegations and proven legal findings
The lessons for any economy: transparency, independent oversight, and accountable public spending

⏱ CHAPTERS
0:00 The question
0:30 The rise of the New Order
1:45 The system of favoritism
3:30 The hidden economic cost
5:00 The 1997–98 financial crisis
6:45 The fall
7:45 The lesson
9:00 Final question

📚 SOURCES & FURTHER READING

Transparency International, Global Corruption Report 2004
World Bank, Indonesia poverty and economic data
IMF and World Bank analyses of the 1997–98 Asian financial crisis

⚠️ NOTE
This video is for educational purposes. Figures cited are estimates, and allegations are not the same as proven legal findings. Suharto died in 2008 without a criminal corruption conviction.

In this episode of **BizNez Stories**, we break down the real economics of owning an ice cream shop in Texas, including startup costs, monthly revenue, employee wages, rent, inventory, seasonal demand, and operating expenses.

snippet.title: How China Went From Poor to Global Economic Power | Documentary
snippet.description:
How China Went From Poor to Global Economic Power | Documentary



In 1978, China was still a relatively poor country recovering from decades of political and economic upheaval.

Today, it is one of the most powerful economic forces on Earth.

So how did China transform its economy on such an extraordinary scale?

The answer was not one sudden revolution.

China changed its economic system gradually — experimenting with reforms, opening selected parts of the country to foreign investment, expanding infrastructure, and connecting hundreds of millions of workers to global markets.

The transformation began with changes in agriculture and the household responsibility system. Then came the Special Economic Zones, including Shenzhen, which became laboratories for China's new economic model.

Globalization accelerated the process.

China expanded manufacturing, ports, roads, railways and cities while increasingly becoming part of global supply chains. Then in 2001, China joined the World Trade Organization, deepening its integration with the global economy.

But China's rise was about more than cheap labor.

The deeper story was its ability to keep moving up the economic ladder — from agriculture to manufacturing, infrastructure and heavy industry, and eventually sophisticated manufacturing, technology and global supply chains.

This documentary explores the system behind China's extraordinary transformation and how a relatively poor country became a central force in the world economy.

From reform to globalization, from Shenzhen to the WTO, this is the story of how China turned economic experimentation and scale into global power.

The Uncovered Documentary explores the history, economics and strategy behind the world's greatest transformations.

snippet.title: the $2 Trillion loan market nobody is allowed to see #documentary #economics  #explained #finance
snippet.description:
Private credit is a roughly $2 trillion loan market that doesn't appear on any stock exchange. It's how companies borrow when they can't — or won't — go to a bank or a public bond market. And your pension may be one of its lenders.
This film follows the money: from a pension fund's allocation, into a private credit fund, into a company you've never heard of. Why the loans are valued at numbers nobody outside the fund can verify. Why an interest payment can be quietly added to the principal instead of paid. And who gets to act first when a business starts to strain.
The sources don't even agree on how big this market is — which is part of the story.
CHAPTERS
0:00 Cold open
0:48 What private credit actually is
2:10 Where the money comes from
3:30 How the loans are priced
5:00 Who can see the strain first
7:00 The thing nobody can measure
(Update these timestamps to your final cut.)
SOURCES
PwC Private Credit Survey 2026 · Financial Stability Board, Report on Vulnerabilities in Private Credit (May 2026) · European Parliament briefing on private credit market structure (2026) · Morgan Stanley · Cleary Gottlieb · PIMCO
WHAT'S REAL IN THIS VIDEO
Every figure is sourced, and where the sources conflict we say so. Market size estimates ranged from $1.5–2 trillion (FSB) to over $2 trillion (PwC) to ~$2.3 trillion in AUM (European Parliament, 2025). That disagreement is deliberate — it's on screen.

snippet.title: Amazon Open Box Delivery – Avoid Fraud & Check These Things First

In this video, I’ll explain the Amazon Open Box Delivery process, what to check during delivery and how you can reduce the chances of receiving a wrong, damaged or suspicious product.

In this video:
• What is Amazon Open Box Delivery?
• How Open Box Delivery works
• What happens during delivery?
• When should you share the delivery OTP?
• Check the package before opening
• Record the complete unboxing
• Check phone and box condition
• Check seals and accessories

snippet.title: Online Scam? Report It FAST! 🚨 The First 20 Minutes Matter | #Shorts #cybersecurity  #onlinesafety
snippet.description:
🚨 Online Scam? Report It Immediately! The First 20 Minutes Matter!

Have you ever wondered what you should do immediately after becoming a victim of an online scam? ⚠️ In the digital world, every second can matter when dealing with cyber fraud, UPI scams, online banking fraud, and unauthorized transactions.

If money has been stolen from your bank account through a **UPI payment scam, fake investment scheme, phishing link, OTP fraud, credit card fraud, or other online financial scam**, acting quickly may improve the chances of stopping or tracing the transaction. However, **there is no guarantee that your money will be recovered within 20 minutes**. The sooner you report the incident, the better.

🇮🇳 **What should you do after an online financial scam in India?**

✅ Step 1: Immediately call India's Cyber Crime Helpline at **1930** to report financial cyber fraud.

✅ Step 2: Visit the official National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: https://cybercrime.gov.in/

✅ Step 3: Contact your bank or payment service provider immediately and report the unauthorized transaction. Ask them whether the transaction can be stopped, frozen, or disputed.

✅ Step 4: Save all evidence, including transaction IDs, screenshots, phone numbers, WhatsApp chats, payment receipts, suspicious links, and other relevant details.

✅ Step 5: Never share your OTP, UPI PIN, banking password, CVV, or remote-access permissions with anyone claiming they can recover your stolen money.

⚠️ Important warning: Scammers sometimes contact victims again, pretending to be cybercrime officers, bank employees, or recovery agents. They may demand an advance payment to recover the stolen money. Be careful—these can be recovery scams.

In this YouTube Short, we explain why immediate reporting matters, how to report online fraud in India, and which official channels you can use to take action after a cybercrime incident.

📢 Share this video with your friends and family. Awareness is one of the strongest ways to protect yourself from digital fraud.

snippet.title: How a Deepfake Video Call Scammed Arup Out of $25 Million
snippet.description:
A fake AI video call led to a shocking $25 million fraud. And the people on the screen weren't who they appeared to be. 😱

In January 2024, a finance employee at global engineering company Arup was tricked into transferring approximately $25.6 million after receiving instructions from people impersonating senior executives during a fraudulent video conference.

The scammers used deepfake technology, manipulated faces, and fake voices to make the meeting appear legitimate.

The result? 15 money transfers to five bank accounts.

This real-world AI deepfake scam reveals a dangerous reality: seeing someone's face and hearing their voice on a video call is no longer enough to confirm their identity.

💡 The lesson: Always verify unusual financial requests through a separate, trusted communication channel—even when the person appears to be someone you know.

📲 Share this video with someone who handles money or important financial transactions.

🔔 Subscribe for simple, powerful lessons about artificial intelligence, AI safety, and emerging technology.

- What those error messages really mean
- The gadgets, apps and tricks nobody explains properly

From Gemini 4 Argon and Meta Muse Wonder to GPT-6, AI agents, voice AI, and Microsoft's new AI chips, these are the biggest AI updates you need to know this week.

snippet.title: I Tested 8 AI Tools for Fake References and AI Hallucinations. Which One Actually Tells the Truth
snippet.description:
Can AI be trusted to generate academic references? I tested 8 popular AI tools to find out which one produces the most reliable references — and the results were not what I expected.

In this experiment, I gave ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini, Perplexity, Consensus, Jenni AI, SciSpace and DeepSeek the same research prompt and asked them to generate academic references on artificial intelligence and information literacy among university students.

I then copied the references generated by each AI tool into GPTZero's Hallucination Detector to check how many appeared to be authentic, unverifiable or potentially incorrect.

But I didn't stop with AI detection. I also manually checked some of the references using Google and academic search sources because an AI detector can also make mistakes.

The results reveal an important lesson about using AI for academic research: a reference can look completely legitimate and still need to be verified.

snippet.title: I Tested a Free AI Website With 400+ Tools — Is It Actually Free?
snippet.description:
I found a website claiming to offer 400+ AI tools in one place — including AI chat, image generation, video generation, music, text-to-speech, speech-to-text, coding, and more.

But how much of it is actually free?

I tested Free.ai using one free account, without paying for credits or adding external API keys. I tracked the token usage before and after my tests and tested the actual results instead of simply trusting the website's claims.

I tested:

• AI Chat
• AI Image Generation
• Text-to-Speech
• Speech-to-Text
• AI Video Generation
• Token usage
• Free daily limits
• Overall quality and usability

The results were mixed. Some tools were usable, while others had major problems. I also found a significant discrepancy between the token usage shown in the chat interface and the usage shown in my account history.

The free plan advertises 30,000 tokens per day, but also limits users to 1 video, 2 songs, and 5 images per day.

The video generator was particularly problematic, costing 15,000 tokens for a 3-second video after an extremely long queue.

So can Free.ai actually replace multiple AI tools with one free website?

I tested it to find out.

Final Scores

Chat — 5/10
Image — 0/10
TTS — 8/10
Speech-to-text — 8/10
Video — 0/10

**Overall — 21/50**

snippet.title: Sudowrite Surprises Us! 😲 AI Writing Tools Tested | Aaila AI Ep.16Aaila AI16
snippet.description:
Welcome to Aaila AI Episode 16 – Writing Tools Continued! ✍️🤖

In Episode 15, we explored Grammarly, JotBot, QuillBot, Copy.ai, and Jasper. In this episode, we continue our journey through AI Writing Tools by testing three more platforms:

🚀 Rytr
📚 Sudowrite
🔍 Writesonic

As always, we're not simply looking at feature lists. We explore real user experience, usability, practical applications, output quality, differentiation, and whether the tool actually offers enough value to justify using it over general-purpose AI tools.

🚀 Rytr

USP: AI-assisted writing with different tones and styles.

Our Test

We used Rytr to create a 2,500-word WhatsApp outreach campaign for a web development prospect, targeting B2C conversion with a convincing tone.

The initial prompt overshot our required length, so we refined it to 2,300 characters and generated multiple variants.

Our Observation

The output was reasonable and comparable to what you can get from general-purpose LLMs such as ChatGPT or Claude.

⭐ Aaila AI Rating: 2/5

Verdict: Useful AI writing assistant, but we didn't find a strong enough differentiator to justify choosing it over a capable general-purpose LLM.

📚 Sudowrite

USP: Structured AI assistance specifically designed for creative and long-form fiction writing.

This was the standout tool of the episode. ⭐

Features Explored

📖 Story Bible
• Character profiles
• Motivations
• Inner conflicts
• Dialogue development

💡 Brain Dump
• Capture raw ideas
• Convert ideas into structured concepts

📚 Novel Outline

We created a science-fiction story involving consciousness, souls, multiple timelines, and a hidden threat to humanity.

✅ Character and story development

My most popular tutorial series is "the donut", which is a beginner tutorial where you learn Blender while making a donut. I remake it for each major Blender version change (4.0, 5.0 etc). 

I am also founder and CEO of Poliigon (https://www.poliigon.com) which is a library of premium Textures, HDRIs and Models, used by hundreds of studios worldwide.

In 2024 I moved to the United States with my family, and currently live in The Woodlands Texas with my wife and two children.

snippet.title: Inside Major Corporate Accounting Scandals | Bigger Than Enron (full documentary) | FRONTLINE (PBS)
snippet.description:
Enron’s spectacular collapse in the early 2000s was at the time the biggest financial scandal in U.S. history. It didn’t happen in a vacuum — and it revealed systemic problems far beyond a single company. (Aired 2002)

This journalism is made possible by viewers like you. Donate to FRONTLINE now: https://bit.ly/47DFzCb

And support your local PBS station here: https://www.pbs.org/donate

In the 2002 documentary “Bigger Than Enron,” Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Hedrick Smith looked at Enron’s implosion and asked, “Where were the watchdogs who were supposed to warn us when companies were playing fast and loose with their books — the stock analysts, lawyers, bankers, Securities and Exchange Commission? Above all, where were the accountants?”

“Bigger Than Enron” investigated those questions in detail, offering an in-depth look at where the U.S. financial regulation landscape stood in June 2002 after Enron’s collapse. 
The documentary is now streaming on YouTube for the first time as part of an effort to make FRONTLINE’s multi-decade reporting archive widely accessible.  

In the film, experts told Smith that what happened at Enron — a cozy collaboration between the company and its accounting firm, Arthur Andersen, that enabled Enron to overstate its profits — was far from anomalous. Smith reported that in what was described as the “go-go ‘90s,” the drive for profits was in full swing, and big accounting firms regularly worked hand-in-glove with clients and Wall Street to find loopholes in accounting rules that made companies look more successful than they really were.

“This is day-to-day business operations in accounting firms and on Wall Street,” Lynn Turner, a former Wall Street partner at an accounting firm before becoming the SEC's chief accountant, said of such practices at the time. “There is nothing extraordinary, nothing unusual in that respect, with respect to Enron.”

“Bigger Than Enron” examined three specific cases involving Andersen where misleading or fraudulent accounting practices caused enormous investor losses — at Sunbeam, Waste Management, and finally, Enron — and explored the downfall of Andersen, a firm that had previously built its reputation on rock-ribbed integrity.

The documentary also looked at how, in the decade leading up to Enron, accounting and financial industry lobbyists had successfully flexed their muscle on Capitol Hill in three battles: the fight over tort reform, the fight over stock options, and the war over a SEC attempt to rein in conflicts of interest by forcing accounting firms to separate their auditing and consulting practices.

Visit pbs.org/frontline to read about legal and regulatory developments since this documentary aired, including the Supreme Court’s 2005 overturning of Arthur Andersen’s obstruction of justice conviction.

“Bigger Than Enron” was a FRONTLINE coproduction with Hedrick Smith Productions. The writer, producer and director was Marc Shaffer. The producer and correspondent was Hedrick Smith. The executive editor of FRONTLINE was Louis Wiley Jr. The executive producer of FRONTLINE was David Fanning. 
#Documentary #Enron #WallStreet #Finance

snippet.title: Ford's Biggest Failure Became a Collector's Dream 🚗 #shorts #mystery  #truestory  #documentary
snippet.description:
🚗 In 1958, Ford introduced the Edsel, promoting it as the "car of the future" and investing millions into one of the biggest product launches in automotive history.

But despite the massive marketing campaign, customers criticized its styling, quality issues emerged, and an economic recession reduced demand for new cars. Within just a few years, the Edsel was discontinued, costing Ford hundreds of millions of dollars and earning a reputation as one of the greatest product failures in business history.

Ironically, the Edsel's story didn't end there. Today, surviving models are prized by collectors and have become iconic pieces of automotive history.

💬 Do you think the Edsel failed because of its design, bad timing, or unrealistic expectations? Share your opinion in the comments!

📌 Follow Red Discover for more fascinating business failures, historical events, and unbelievable true stories.

snippet.title: Rise and Fall of Nokia: World's Biggest Mobile Failure | Case Study
snippet.description:
#Rise and Fall of Nokia: World's Biggest Mobile Failure | Case Study

Once upon a time, Nokia was the king of the mobile phone industry. From the legendary Nokia 3310 to the iconic Nokia ringtone, the brand became a part of millions of lives, especially in India. But how did the world's most dominant mobile phone company lose its leadership?

Many people believe that Apple and Android killed Nokia. But the real story goes much deeper. From rejected touchscreen phone prototypes to internal corporate pressure, delayed decisions, and a controversial partnership with Microsoft, Nokia's downfall is one of the most fascinating business stories in the history of technology.

In this **business documentary**, we uncover the untold story behind the rise and fall of Nokia and explore the critical decisions that changed the future of the mobile phone industry forever.

In this detailed **business case study**, you'll discover:

- **Nokia's Rise:** How a Finnish company that originally started in the paper industry became a global mobile phone giant.
- **Nokia 3310 and the Nokia Ringtone:** How durable phones, long battery life, and iconic branding helped Nokia win millions of customers.
- **Steve Jobs iPhone Launch:** How Apple's revolutionary iPhone changed consumer expectations and transformed the smartphone industry.
- **Why Nokia Failed:** The internal problems, software challenges, slow decision-making, and missed opportunities that weakened Nokia.
- **The Hidden Touchscreen Project:** How Nokia engineers reportedly developed touchscreen phone concepts years before the iPhone arrived.
- **Nokia's Business Strategy:** Why the company moved away from Symbian and chose Microsoft's Windows Phone instead of Android.
- **The Stephen Elop Controversy:** Understanding the controversial decisions, the Microsoft connection, and the unproven theories surrounding Nokia's decline.
- **The Microsoft Deal:** How Nokia sold its mobile phone business and why Microsoft's attempt to revive the business also struggled.
- **Why Companies Fail:** The business lessons Nokia's story teaches us about innovation, leadership, employee communication, and adapting to technological change.
- **Nokia Today:** How the company survived by shifting its focus toward telecommunications networks and infrastructure.

This business story is not just about a mobile phone company losing its position. It is about how even the biggest companies can struggle when they fail to adapt to a changing market.

The rise and fall of Nokia offers important lessons in business history, business strategy, leadership, innovation, and competition. If you enjoy business stories, corporate failures, technology documentaries, and real-world case study analysis, this video will help you understand what went wrong inside one of the world's most famous brands.

**Was Nokia destroyed by the iPhone, Android, or its own internal decisions?** Watch till the end to understand why the answer is more complicated than most people think.

snippet.title: Why Short Ads Fail in Business: Inside the Branded Documentary Model
snippet.description:
How do you turn corporate messaging into authentic human connection, build trust with high-stakes audiences, and elevate your brand through cinematic storytelling?

In this episode of Audacity of Entrepreneurs, Nick Uresin sits down with William Kruse, founder and creative director of Clever. William shares his perspective on documentary filmmaking, motion content strategy, long-form branded storytelling, and the irreplaceable value of human connection in an increasingly AI-driven market.

Together, they explore how business leaders can bridge the gap between entertainment-quality media and commercial marketing to build long-term authority and customer loyalty.

William Kruse is a former filmmaker with nearly two decades of experience in independent cinema, production, and creative direction. Through Clever, he helps healthcare and medtech brands create series-based short documentaries that connect deeply with patients and physicians alike. Combining a background in film theory from Notre Dame and industry production from Florida State, William brings a rare mix of artistic vision, strategic messaging, and execution discipline to modern brand strategy.

William explains that true audience engagement comes down to authentic human stories rather than pitch-heavy commercial spots. He breaks down how dropping into cities to shoot broadcast-quality series in 48 hours creates high-value brand assets, why longer runtimes serve information-hungry audiences in regulated spaces, and how documentary archetypes allow viewers to see themselves in your message. He also takes a passionate stand on the front lines of the creative response to AI, advocating for genuine human empathy in visual media.

In this episode, you'll discover:

- Why standard corporate video fails and how documentary principles fill the gap
- How to bridge the divide between commercial marketing and independent filmmaking
- The power of series-based content for sustained audience engagement and touchpoints
- Why high-stakes industries (like healthcare) require longer-form, information-rich storytelling
- How high-end broadcast production values instantly elevate brand authority
- The mechanics of motion content strategy, production, and activation
- Why conducting deep audience research before writing a script guarantees high engagement
- How executing 48-hour sight-unseen shoots builds high-impact content on tight schedules
- Why human intelligence and authentic connection will outlast automated creative AI
- How documenting real human experiences leaves a lasting business and visual legacy

If you're an entrepreneur, marketing executive, agency leader, or brand strategist, this conversation is packed with practical lessons about choosing the right content format, overcoming market friction, engaging complex audiences, and building a brand that stands out.

Whether you're launching your first startup or leading an established company, this conversation is packed with practical strategies you can implement immediately.

There was a time when owning a BlackBerry meant you had made it.

Its physical keyboard was iconic. Its messaging service changed how people communicated. And its phones became essential tools for business leaders, professionals, and millions of everyday users.

But then the smartphone revolution arrived — and the company that once helped define the future of mobile technology struggled to keep up.

What went wrong? Was BlackBerry too confident in its success? Did it underestimate touchscreen smartphones? Or did its biggest weakness come from decisions made long before its decline became obvious?

In this episode of **Simplify It**, we uncover the story behind BlackBerry's rise, its dominance in mobile communication, the challenges that threatened its position, and the strategic decisions that contributed to its downfall.

From its famous physical keyboard and secure messaging to its struggle against changing consumer expectations and competing smartphone platforms, this is a story about innovation, competition, leadership, and the danger of standing still in a fast-moving industry.

- How BlackBerry became a major force in mobile communication
- Why its physical keyboard and messaging features were so popular
- How BlackBerry built a loyal customer base
- How touchscreen smartphones changed the industry
- Why software and apps became increasingly important

### ⏱️ Video Chapters

Why did BlackBerry disappear? Explore the rise and fall of the mobile giant that once defined connectivity and secure communication.

Before the modern era of touchscreens, BlackBerry was the standard for business professionals. The company built a reputation on security and physical keyboards, becoming a dominant force in the mobile phone industry. snippet.title: Kodak Saw the Digital Future. So Why Did It Fail? #documentary #Kodak #future
snippet.description:
In 1975, Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built something extraordinary: a camera that could take pictures without using film.

It was about the size of a toaster, weighed around 8 pounds, and took 23 seconds to record a single image onto a cassette tape.

Yet decades later, Kodak — the company behind this invention — filed for bankruptcy.

So what happened?

Did Kodak fail to see the future, or did it see the digital revolution coming and struggle to adapt?

In this cinematic mini-documentary, we explore the story of Kodak's first digital camera, the engineer who built it, the decisions that shaped the company's future, and the business challenges behind one of photography's most fascinating stories.

This isn't simply a story about a company that failed. It's a story about innovation, business strategy, technological disruption, and the difficult decisions that can shape the future of an entire industry.

🎬 IN THIS DOCUMENTARY

- The invention of Kodak's digital camera in 1975
- Steven Sasson and his remarkable prototype
- Why Kodak's leadership faced a difficult decision
- How Kodak entered the digital camera market
- The business challenges behind Kodak's decline
- What happened when Kodak filed for bankruptcy in 2012

snippet.title: Polaroid Went Bankrupt in 2001. The Film Came Back | Business Documentary
snippet.description:
The original Polaroid company went bankrupt in 2001, and the later one filed in December 2008, yet in April 2025 Polaroid announced a new camera.
So how did Polaroid's instant film come back?
The story runs through a pair of sunglasses, a button that made waiting disappear, and a film factory in the Netherlands.
1972. Polaroid's SX-70 brings camera and film together as one experience, without the old peel-apart step.

snippet.title: How Enron Made Its Money: An Enron Documentary
snippet.description:
This Enron documentary asks the question a Fortune reporter put to Enron in March 2001: how exactly did it make its money? From the 1992 accounting rule that let Enron book a contract's whole future profit on paper to its bankruptcy on December 2, 2001, this Enron documentary follows the answer.

How did Enron fail? It reported more than 100 billion dollars in revenue, but much of its growth came from profits booked in advance from its own forecasts, gains from partnerships run by its own finance chief, and debts kept off its balance sheet, so when the share price fell, the structures holding it up fell with it.

We follow Jeffrey Skilling's Gas Bank idea, Andrew Fastow's LJM and Raptor partnerships, a Blockbuster streaming trial that produced about 110 million dollars of reported profit, Bethany McLean's question in Fortune and Sherron Watkins' warning letter, through the 47 days that ended the company. The Enron scandal also brought down the accounting firm Arthur Andersen, and the Enron bankruptcy led straight to the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.

Watch next: Inside the Wirecard Scandal: Germany's €1.9 Billion Gap — https://youtu.be/qu3FK_Uj43s

snippet.title: Netflix Offered to Sell Itself for $50 Million. #history #shortsfeed #animateddocumentary
snippet.description:
Netflix once tried to sell itself to Blockbuster for $50 million. Blockbuster said no, and a decade later it was bankrupt. But that is only half of the story.

This is the rise and fall of Blockbuster, the video rental giant that lost to a DVD-by-mail startup. In 2000, Netflix was a small company losing money. The story goes that Reed Hastings flew to Dallas with a simple pitch: Blockbuster runs the stores, and Netflix runs Blockbuster online. The legend says the room barely held back its laughter at the idea of paying $50 million for a mail-order DVD site. Blockbuster passed.

It makes a perfect business myth: an arrogant giant that laughed at the future. But the legend skips the second half. Blockbuster's own CEO pushed the company into online rentals. The problem was late fees, which fed a huge share of the profits. Going online meant dropping them, and that created a fight inside the company. In 2007, he left after clashing with the board. Three years later, Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy. Today, only a single Blockbuster store remains, in Bend, Oregon.

So what really killed Blockbuster? Was it one bad decision, the late fees, a boardroom fight, or the shift to streaming? In this video, we break down the timeline, the decisions and the mistakes behind one of the most famous company collapses in business history, and we name the real cause of death.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN
- Why the famous $50 million story is more complicated than the legend
- How late fees shaped Blockbuster's strategy
- How a boardroom clash changed the company's fate
- Why big companies lose to startups
- What Blockbuster's collapse teaches about brand history and business mistakes

snippet.title: iPHONE INDICATOR DOTS EXPLAINED! 🍎🔍#iPhoneTips #AppleTips #iOSTips #TechFacts#shorts#trendingshorts
snippet.description:
📱 iPHONE INDICATOR DOTS EXPLAINED! 🍎🔍

Did you know what those tiny colored dots on your iPhone mean? 🤔

These indicator lights help you understand when apps are accessing certain features of your iPhone. 🚀

🟠 Orange Dot: An app is using your microphone. 🎙️
🟢 Green Dot: An app is using your camera (sometimes along with the microphone). 📸
🔴 Red Dot: May indicate screen recording or recording-related activity, depending on the iOS version and feature. 🔴
🔵 Blue Indicator: Can appear when certain system features or apps are actively using location services. 📍

💡 Pro Tip: If you notice an indicator unexpectedly, check your iPhone's Control Center to see which app recently accessed your camera or microphone. You can also review app permissions in Settings.

🔥 Save this post for future reference and share it with your tech-loving friends!

snippet.title: USB Drive Buying Explained!? 😲
snippet.description:
Before you buy your next USB drive, here's what actually matters — because a lot of cheap or fake USB drives on the market look identical to the real thing, but fail fast or perform way worse than advertised.

In this video, I cover the exact checklist to follow before buying a USB flash drive:

Stick to a reputable brand — SanDisk, Kingston, and similar trusted names. Unbranded or no-name drives are where most problems start.
Check the actual transfer speed before buying, not just the label on the box.
Make sure it's USB 3.0 or higher — older USB versions are noticeably slower for transferring larger files.
Always buy with a warranty, so if the drive fails, you can actually get it replaced instead of losing your money.
Avoid fake or counterfeit USB drives entirely — they're not only slower than advertised, they also tend to fail much sooner.
Don't just trust the storage capacity printed on the packaging — fake drives are known for showing capacities way higher than what they actually hold. Check reviews if you're unsure.

🔧 What you'll learn in this video:

How to spot a fake or counterfeit USB drive
Which USB version you should be buying (and why)
Why warranty matters when buying storage devices
How to avoid overpaying for a drive that underperforms

If you've been searching for how to buy a USB flash drive, best USB drive brands, how to spot a fake flash drive, or USB 3.0 vs USB 2.0 — this video covers it.

snippet.description:
🔊 How to Connect 3 Speakers in Series | Speaker Wiring Explained

In this video, you will learn how to connect 3 speakers in series and understand how series wiring works in an audio system.

⚡ What You Will Learn: ✅ How to connect 3 speakers in series ✅ Speaker series wiring explained ✅ How series connection affects total impedance (ohms) ✅ How speaker impedance affects an amplifier ✅ Understanding speaker wattage and power distribution ✅ Important precautions when connecting multiple speakers

🎯 Important Note: When speakers are connected in series, their impedances add together. The total impedance must be compatible with your amplifier's supported load. The power received by each speaker depends on its impedance, the amplifier output, and the speaker characteristics. Speaker wattage ratings do not simply add up to determine the actual output power.

snippet.title: Every NIGHTMARE Tech FAIL Explained 14 Minutes!
snippet.description:
Exploding phones, melting GPUs, drives that earned the nickname "Deathstar," and a CPU that couldn't do basic math — the tech industry has produced some spectacular disasters over the decades. This detailed breakdown covers fourteen of the worst hardware and engineering failures in computing history, from Samsung's Galaxy Note 7 recall to Apple's dust-defeated butterfly keyboard, with every technical cause explained in plain language.

Each failure tells a bigger story about what happens when companies chase thinner designs, higher clock speeds, or misleading spec sheets instead of getting the fundamentals right. Whether it was Nvidia quietly shipping a mislabeled GPU, Intel betting everything on a dead-end architecture, or AMD marketing shared modules as full cores, these mistakes cost billions and reshaped entire product lines.


----------------------------------------------------------------------------

snippet.title: How AI Data Centers Are Making Everything More Expensive
snippet.description:
The rapid growth of AI data centers is creating a shortage of the memory chips used in everyday devices like laptops, phones, cameras, and gaming consoles. 

The world's three largest memory chipmakers — SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron — are shifting production to High Bandwidth Memory, specialized microchips that power AI data centers, rather than the DRAM and NAND chips found in many consumer electronics. With fewer traditional chips being produced, tech manufacturers are paying more for components and passing the costs to customers through higher prices.

Read "I used Claude to solve a problem that data centers helped cause for my photography business. It's saved me thousands": https://bit.ly/3SHI29M

snippet.title: 5G Hard Gold New in India | Business | Sarthak Ahuja
snippet.description:
A new kind of gold has come into the Indian market called the 5D Hard Gold and the Electroformed Hollow Gold...

It’s a new technology which has seen success in China and is now entering India as a new way of making gold jewellery...

Now because of rising gold rates, jewellers are trying to make gold jewellery, which is hollow and thin, but looks big...

the problem with the current technology is that they make gold jewellery by pouring gold over wax moulds, but thin jewellery ends up getting dented very quickly...

With this new technique of electroforming, after the wax moulds are made, they are put into a machine that does microplating of gold on top of the moulds... like electric currents building a hard shell outside of the mould...

These particles harden much more than poured gold, and jewellers are also able to make hard jewellery out of 24K gold using this method... as this method allows them to create gold almost up to 4X as hard...

Plus, it allows them to make very intricate jewellery that is otherwise difficult to do, and do things like mirror finishes... using up to 60% lesser gold compared to the traditional method...

So what would otherwise take 20 grams of gold, can be made in just 8 grams through this method...

This gold is called 3D Hard Gold... when they do mirror finishes and other such improvements on the finish, it starts being called 5D Hard Gold...

This technology has been patented in China since 2009, but has started coming into commercial use now that gold prices are through the roof...

A lot of this machinery is being imported from China... and some suppliers in India say that it can cost anywhere between Rs 80 Lakhs to over Rs 5 crore if you wish to set up an industrial line...

As the market develops, the moat will be in jewellers learning this skill and making more intricate designs to beat their competition...

As for consumers, the making charges on these designs may be higher but would result in more unique pieces...

snippet.title: Why ITC Is Entering AI Business? Happiest Minds Deal Explained
snippet.description:
ITC is making a major move beyond its traditional businesses of cigarettes, FMCG, hotels and paper by investing ₹1,330 crore in Happiest Minds Technologies.

But is ITC becoming a technology company?

Not exactly.

The bigger story is that ITC is trying to build a new AI-focused technology growth engine through ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds.

In this video, we explain:

Why ITC invested ₹1,330 crore in Happiest Minds
How the ITC Infotech and Happiest Minds merger will work
Why AI is changing the IT services industry
What Happiest Minds brings to ITC Infotech
What ITC Infotech adds to the combined business
Why AI implementation could create new opportunities for IT companies
Can the combined company become a $1 billion revenue business by FY28?

Under the deal:

ITC Infotech will acquire around 22.1% stake in Happiest Minds
Deal value is around ₹1,330 crore
Happiest Minds will merge with ITC Infotech
The combined company aims to build stronger capabilities in AI, digital engineering, cloud, cybersecurity and data services

Happiest Minds brings expertise in:

Generative AI
Cloud transformation
Cybersecurity
Digital engineering
Data and IoT solutions

ITC Infotech brings:

Large enterprise relationships
Industry expertise across manufacturing, consumer goods, BFSI, travel and hospitality
Existing technology service capabilities

The IT industry is changing. Earlier companies mainly focused on coding support and outsourcing. Today, businesses need technology partners that can help them implement AI, modernise legacy systems, manage cloud infrastructure and improve cybersecurity.

For ITC investors, this deal is not about immediate earnings. The bigger question is whether ITC Infotech can successfully convert AI capabilities into meaningful revenue growth.

Investors should track:

Can the combined company achieve the $1 billion revenue target?
Can AI transformation deals convert into actual revenue?
Can merger synergies improve margins?

snippet.title: SFC Environmental Technologies IPO 2026: Issue Size, Price Band & Business Explained #ipo #share
snippet.description:
SFC Environmental Technologies IPO: The business behind wastewater treatment and waste-to-energy.

SFC Environmental Technologies provides solutions for wastewater treatment, recycling, reuse and solid waste management. Its proprietary C-Tech technology is used in wastewater treatment, while its OREX technology helps process municipal waste for biogas generation and resource recovery.

The company has commissioned 728 wastewater treatment installations and operates across 23 states and 5 Union Territories. Its expansion into wastewater recycling and compressed biogas projects adds another dimension to its business.

IPO Details
• Issue Size: ₹667.53 crore
• Price Band: ₹313–330 per share
• Fresh Issue: ₹150 crore
• Offer for Sale (OFS): ₹517.53 crore
• Subscription Dates: 27–29 October 2026
• Lot Size: 45 shares
• Tentative Listing: 3 November 2026

Where will the money go?

The company plans to use approximately ₹42.23 crore from the fresh issue to repay borrowings and ₹74.92 crore to meet working capital requirements. The remaining proceeds are earmarked for general corporate purposes. The OFS portion, meanwhile, goes to selling shareholders rather than the company.

What should investors watch?

The business operates in a sector linked to environmental infrastructure and wastewater management. However, its dependence on government projects and tenders, customer concentration, and working capital requirements are important risks to evaluate before investing.

An IPO is not automatically a good investment just because the sector has growth potential. Read the RHP and assess the risks before making a decision.

CRED looks like a simple credit-card bill payment and rewards app. But the real business model is much bigger.

In this episode of Prince Builds — Tech Decoder, we break down how CRED makes money and why rewarding users can actually be a powerful business strategy.

When you pay your credit-card bill through CRED, the reward isn't necessarily the business itself.

It helps CRED attract a valuable audience of financially active and creditworthy users. From there, CRED can build a larger ecosystem around financial products, payments, lending, insurance, lifestyle and brand partnerships.

CRED itself says its platform serves 17 million monthly members and spans payments, lending, insurance, wealth and lifestyle products.

CRED itself says its platform serves 17 million monthly members and spans payments, lending, insurance, wealth and lifestyle products.

And its partner platform explicitly pitches brands on direct access to CRED's high-value customer base.

snippet.title: Business Insider
snippet.description:

Our videos break down how industries operate, how decisions get made, and how power and money move across the globe. We report on the companies, people, and trends shaping the world — and explain what it means for your work, money, and future. We publish videos weekly.

snippet.title: Sarthak Ahuja
snippet.description:
Helping businesses go global.

I’m Sarthak Ahuja, an investment banker, business educator and 4X author. On this channel, I break down what it really takes to grow a business across borders.

🎓 Business Class: Explainers on doing business with different countries. Markets, trade, regulation and where the opportunities are.

🎙️ Founder’s Office: Conversations with founders and operators across industries about how they expanded internationally.

About me: CA, CS, CMA, BFIA, MBA. Gold Medalist from the Indian School of Business (ISB), where I now teach Corporate Finance, and visiting faculty at other leading business schools. I have over a decade of experience in deal advisory and corporate finance, and I sit on the advisory boards of startups across India and the Middle East.

New videos every week.

snippet.title: 7 Grok Bot agents I use every day
snippet.description:
I’m running about 30 active agents at any given moment, and in this episode I break down my full Grok Bot setup: what it is, how it compares to OpenClaw, and the nine bots I’ve built for work and my personal life. We go deep on Chief (my chief-of-staff bot sweeping six inboxes and multiple Slack workspaces), TradBot (the family agent that prints a kitchen-table newspaper for my kids), two engineering bots handling my PR queue and SOC 2 compliance monitoring, Holly Helpdesk, and a handful of personal bots I didn’t expect to actually love. I also walk through how I migrated everything from OpenClaw, including the script I used to export and transplant each agent’s identity and schedule.

*What you’ll learn:*
1. The three primitives Grok Bot is built on, and why one of them changes what agents can actually do
2. How Chief, my general-purpose chief of staff, handles a scope I didn’t think a single bot could manage
3. The writing quirk I noticed immediately with the Grok model, and what I did about it before letting it near my inbox
4. Why I created a family agent, what it produces every morning, and the design principle I used that has nothing to do with a screen
5. The two engineering bots doing work I used to do myself, and how one of them handles compliance in a way that surprised me
6. How Holly Helpdesk started getting five-star reviews from customers who had no idea they were talking to a bot
7. The personal bots I built mostly on a whim, and the one I now look forward to every Monday morning

*My bot templates:* https://x.com/clairevo/status/2093496602522714362

*Brought to you by:*
WorkOS—Make your app enterprise-ready, with SSO, SCIM, RBAC, and more: https://workos.com?utm_source=lennys_howiai&utm_medium=podcast&utm_campaign=q22025
Hyperagent—Deploy fleets of agents that handle real work: https://www.hyperagent.com/howiai

*In this episode, we cover:*

snippet.title: Small businesses are obsessed with AI slop...
snippet.description:
Start your own store for free with #Printify: 
https://try.printify.com/47qtqk27k4d7 
Use code LOGICALLY - the first 100 users get 15% off their first order.

Why are small businesses obsessed with AI slop? From uncanny food on restaurant menus to glossy posters that all look the same, AI-generated marketing is everywhere. And honestly, some of it makes the old Canva templates look pretty good. But behind the strange images are owners juggling tight margins, children, and a to-do list that never ends. For many, generating a poster isn't about avoiding a designer. It's about getting one more task done. This video looks at why small businesses are turning to AI, what happened when San Francisco's Grind & Unwind put up AI-generated menus, and why saving time on marketing can create a much bigger problem. We explore how obvious AI ads can make a message harder to understand, why nearly realistic food can feel uncanny, and how customers can read a cheap-looking image as a sign of the product's quality. There's also a brand paradox: small businesses already have the personality that giant chains spend millions trying to create. When every local restaurant starts using the same polished AI look, that advantage starts disappearing. Sometimes, an imperfect photo or a slightly awkward handmade sign says more about a business than glossy AI poster.

I run this episode solo. I explain local AI in plain terms: the model runs on hardware I control, and a cloud model runs somewhere else. I map the four pieces of the local AI landscape — the model, the warehouse, the software, and the workflow — and I define the words that beginners meet first: parameters, tokens, context window, quantization, and GGUF. I walk through the Google open model stack (Gemma 4, Google AI Edge, LiteRT-LM, AI Edge Gallery), compare the other open model families, and show three ways to run a model today. I close with a first workflow you can copy and three startup ideas that use local AI as the wedge.

And a special thank you to Google for supporting the podcast. 

Get the full guide to running local AI: https://startup-ideas-pod.link/local-ai

00:00 – Intro
01:35 – The Open Model the Landscape
03:09 – Vocab Decoder
06:48 – Google Gemma Clearly Explained
10:29 – Other Open Model Families
14:20 – Path 1: Run Gemma in LM Studio
18:17 – Path 2: Ollama
20:15 – Path 3: Google AI Edge

22:47 – Workflows Before Fine-Tuning
25:06 – Local vs Cloud vs Hybrid Eval
26:33 – Framework for Local AI Startup Ideas
27:22 – Startup Idea 1: Home Health QA Reviewer
29:24 – Startup Idea 2: Offline Field Report Copilot
32:10 – Startup Idea 3: Pre-Send Reviewer for Professional Services
34:47 – Build Your Local AI Lab
37:55 – Closing Thoughts

Key Points

• Ask whether the model is good enough for the job, and the business opportunities become clear.
• Local AI has four pieces: the model, the warehouse (Hugging Face), the software (LM Studio or Ollama), and the workflow you build around them.
• Gemma 4 E4B is my practical starting point; E2B fits phones and older machines.
• Hybrid architecture wins: local does the private first pass, cloud does the heavy reasoning, and a human approves anything important.
• Start with one repeated workflow — one folder, one model, one output — and run it 10 times.
• I see a 24-month window to build local-AI-native software for verticals that still run early-2000s tools.

Numbered Section Summaries

1. The Four Pieces of the Local AI Landscape I break the space into the model (the brain file, such as Gemma, Llama, or Mistral), the warehouse (Hugging Face), the software that runs the model (LM Studio or Ollama), and the workflow (the product around all of it). Underneath the tools sit Llama.cpp and MLX, and for shipping on-device apps in the Google ecosystem you reach Google AI Edge and LiteRT-LM. On Hugging Face I read a model card slowly and look for six things: purpose, size, license, hardware, supported inputs, and quantized files.

2. The Vocabulary That Matters I define parameters as the internal weights, where more parameters give more capacity and cost more memory: 2B and 4B for edge devices and fast workflows, 12B as a middle ground, and 26B or 31B for workstation territory. I define tokens, the context window, quantization (Q4 for easier running, Q8 for more quality), and GGUF as the common local file format. I suggest you start on a phone or a spare 2021 laptop and keep your money for later.

3. The Google Open Model Stack Gemma is Google's open model family, and Gemma 4 targets efficient local and on-device use across E2B, E4B, 12B, and 26B/31B. The specialized models deserve attention: EmbeddingGemma for search by meaning, FunctionGemma for tool use and structured function calling, PaliGemma for vision, ShieldGemma for safety, and Gemma Scope for interpretability. Around the models sit Google AI Edge, LiteRT-LM, AI Edge Gallery, and Gemini plus Google Cloud for frontier-level reasoning.

4. Three Ways to Run Gemma Today Path one is LM Studio: download the app, search for Gemma 4, pick E4B or E2B, grab the quantized GGUF, and paste real customer notes into a chat to feel the value. Then start the LM Studio local server so your scripts and prototypes call the model through localhost. Path two is Ollama with a local API on port 11434, and path three is Google AI Edge with LiteRT-LM for Android, iOS, web, desktop, and edge apps. I also give a RAM cheat sheet: 8 GB stays small, 16 GB runs useful experiments, 32 GB opens larger workflows, and a strong GPU makes the bigger models realistic.

Through honest conversations with global experts, visionaries, and game-changers, we explore refreshing ideas and mindsets that shape our lives. Whether you’re chasing a dream, navigating change, or simply looking for a new perspective, this is the space for curious, open minds and big ambitions.

snippet.title: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast
snippet.description:
67% of my viewers don't realize they don't subscribe, please double check, thank you!!

I own 7 businesses and 8 RV parks, and I'm here to enable your shiny object syndrome with:

1. Diving deep on unique business ideas and growth hacks.

2. Talking to interesting entrepreneurs and multipreneurs about how their business works and what other business ideas they're excited about.

3. Proving stories and lessons learned the 75+ businesses I've started.

4. Showing you how to invest in mobile home and RV parks.

Always tactical, no fluff to be found. Thanks for joining!
